question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A serpent having many heads in Greek mythology
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Hydra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hydra" is the one-word substitute for a serpent having many heads in Greek mythology. In Greek legend, the Lernaean Hydra was a many-headed water serpent that grew two new heads each time one was cut off. (अनेक सिरों वाला पौराणिक सर्प)

◦ Correct: The Hydra was slain by the hero Heracles as one of his twelve labours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Python" — a large non-venomous constricting snake (also a monstrous serpent slain by Apollo, but not many-headed).

• Option 3 "Cobra" — a venomous hooded snake, an ordinary reptile, not mythological.

• Option 4 "Eopsin" — not a standard English word.

NOTE

• "Hydra" is now also used figuratively for a persistent, many-sided problem that is hard to eradicate (a "hydra-headed" menace).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The plan was very ____________ and took a lot of time to develop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. elaborate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the linking verb "was very", an adjective is required to describe "the plan". "Elaborate" (adjective) means detailed and complicated; carefully worked out. (विस्तृत / जटिल)

◦ Correct: The plan was very elaborate and took a lot of time to develop.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "being elaborate" is grammatically wrong after "was very".

• Option 3 "elaborates" is a verb (present tense), and Option 4 "elaboration" is a noun — neither fits after "very".

NOTE

• "Elaborate" works as both an adjective (an elaborate design) and a verb (to elaborate = to explain in detail). Here the adjective form is needed.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom/phrase.

Throw in the towel
option_2: To cause an activity or process to continue
option_3: To take responsibility for a situation while another person is temporarily absent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To give up or surrender.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "throw in the towel" means to give up or surrender; to admit defeat. It comes from boxing, where a fighter's corner throws a towel into the ring to stop the fight. (हार मान लेना)

◦ Example: After months of losses, the company finally threw in the towel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to prepare to fight" is the opposite sense.

• Options 2 and 3 do not relate to the idiom at all.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of quitting/surrender: "throw in the sponge", "call it a day", "wave the white flag", "give up the ghost".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Whoever got the few answers correct has to leave the room.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. fewest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context requires the superlative — the person who got the fewest (the smallest number of) answers correct. "Fewest" is the superlative of "few" (few – fewer – fewest). (सबसे कम)

◦ Correct: Whoever got the fewest answers correct has to leave the room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fewer" is comparative (used with "than") and needs a second element.

• Option 3 "more fewer" is a double comparative and Option 4 "most few" is non-standard — both are always incorrect.

NOTE

• "Few/fewer/fewest" are used with countable nouns (fewer answers, fewer people); "little/less/least" are used with uncountable nouns (less water).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Please hang with for two minutes while I finish cleaning the utensils.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Please hang with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb here is "hang on" (meaning to wait for a short time), not "hang with". So the segment should be "Please hang on". (थोड़ा रुकना / प्रतीक्षा करना)

◦ Correct: Please hang on for two minutes while I finish cleaning the utensils.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "for two minutes", "while I finish cleaning" and "the utensils" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "hang": hang on (wait), hang up (end a phone call), hang out (spend time), hang around (loiter). Here "hang on" = wait.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym for the word provided in the bracket to fill in the blank.

The professor delivered a ___________________ lecture on quantum physics. (simplified)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Complex.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Simplified" means made easy or less complicated. Its antonym is "complex", meaning complicated and difficult to understand. (सरल का विलोम — जटिल)

◦ Correct: The professor delivered a complex lecture on quantum physics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Refined" (polished/purified) and Option 2 "Plain" (simple) are not antonyms of "simplified".

• Option 3 "Lengthy" refers to length, not complexity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of complex: complicated, intricate, convoluted, elaborate. Antonyms: simple, plain, straightforward, simplified.

question: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
option_1: The sceintist discovered a new palnet in the galaxy.
option_2: The scientist discovred a new planet in the galexy.
option_3: The scientist discovered a new planet in the galaxy.
option_4: The scienetist discovered a new planet in the galaxy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The scientist discovered a new planet in the galaxy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt words are "scientist", "discovered", "planet" and "galaxy".

◦ Correct: The scientist discovered a new planet in the galaxy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "scientist" as "sceintist" and "planet" as "palnet".

• Option 2 misspells "discovered" as "discovred" and "galaxy" as "galexy".

• Option 4 misspells "scientist" as "scienetist".

NOTE

• Spelling tip: "scientist" follows the pattern sci-en-tist ("i before e" exception after "c"); "galaxy" ends in -axy.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The car which I bought last year was cheap than my bike.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. was cheap than my bike.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of "cheap" is "cheaper", so it should be "was cheaper than my bike". (सस्ता का तुलनात्मक रूप — cheaper)

◦ Correct: The car which I bought last year was cheaper than my bike.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The car", "which I bought" and "last year" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• One-syllable adjectives form the comparative by adding "-er" + "than": cheap → cheaper, tall → taller, fast → faster. Never use the positive degree with "than".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Infnite.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Infnite" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "infinite", meaning limitless or endless. (अनंत)

◦ Spelling key: IN + FI + NITE (infinite).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Novelist" (a writer of novels), "Throw" (to hurl) and "Eternal" (everlasting) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: infinite (adjective), infinity (noun), infinitely (adverb). Antonym: finite.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The vegetation in this area of the forest is very dense.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sparse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dense" means thick, closely packed or crowded together. Its antonym is "sparse", meaning thinly spread or scanty. (घना का विलोम — विरल)

◦ Correct: If the vegetation were the opposite of dense, it would be sparse.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Spatial" (relating to space), Option 2 "Spare" (extra/reserve) and Option 3 "Spruce" (neat, or a type of tree) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of dense: thick, compact, crowded. Antonyms: sparse, thin, scattered, scanty.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence.

Her profile was complete on the company website.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. incomplete.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Complete" means whole; having all its parts; finished. Its direct antonym is "incomplete", meaning not whole or unfinished. (पूर्ण का विलोम — अपूर्ण)

◦ Correct: The opposite of "her profile was complete" is "her profile was incomplete".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "uploaded", 2 "created" and 4 "received" describe actions and are not antonyms of "complete".

NOTE

• "Incomplete" is formed with the negative prefix "in-" + complete. Other examples: incorrect, invalid, incapable, insufficient.

question:
Identify the error in the usage of the future tense in the given sentence and choose the correct sentence from the following options.

Parvati finish the painting in one hour.
option_1: Parvati has been finishing the painting in one hour.
option_2: Parvati was finished the painting in one hour.
option_3: Parvati will finish the painting in one hour.
option_4: Parvati had been finishing the painting in one hour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Parvati will finish the painting in one hour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence expresses a future action, so the simple future tense "will + base verb" is required. "Parvati will finish the painting in one hour." (भविष्य काल)

◦ Correct: Parvati will finish the painting in one hour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (present perfect continuous) and Option 4 (past perfect continuous) do not express the future.

• Option 2 "was finished" is a wrong past passive construction.

NOTE

• Simple future = subject + will/shall + V1 (will finish, will go). It is used for actions that will happen later, especially with time expressions like "in one hour", "tomorrow".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which was landing at 5:00 a.m. yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. flight which was landing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The action was a single completed event at a specific past time ("at 5:00 a.m. yesterday"), so the simple past "landed" is required, not the past continuous "was landing". So it should be "flight which landed". (सामान्य भूतकाल — landed)

◦ Correct: My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which landed at 5:00 a.m. yesterday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "My aunt came from", "Switzerland by the" and "at 5:00 a.m. yesterday" are all correct.

NOTE

• Use the simple past for a completed action at a definite past time (landed at 5:00 a.m.); use the past continuous only for an action in progress at that time.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

With the increasing reliance on digital systems, ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is _______________ to protect against online threats.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. paramount.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Paramount" means more important than anything else; supreme. Robust cybersecurity being "paramount" means it is of the utmost importance for protection against online threats. (सर्वोपरि / अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण)

◦ Correct: ... ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is paramount to protect against online threats.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "superfluous" (unnecessary/excess) and Option 2 "extraneous" (irrelevant/external) give the opposite sense.

• Option 3 "impartial" (unbiased) does not fit the context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of paramount: supreme, foremost, chief, pre-eminent, of prime importance. Antonyms: unimportant, secondary, trivial.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Hamper
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hinder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hamper" (as a verb) means to hinder, obstruct or slow down the progress of something. Its closest synonym is "hinder". (बाधा डालना)

◦ Example: Heavy rain hampered/hindered the rescue operations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Gift" — note that a "hamper" as a noun can mean a basket of gifts, but as a verb the synonym is "hinder".

• Option 3 "Irritate" (to annoy) and Option 4 "Pamper" (to indulge) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hamper (verb): hinder, impede, obstruct, hamstring, encumber. Antonyms: help, aid, facilitate, assist.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

(1) We knocked across (2) early on Saturday (3) to enjoy (4) the beautiful weather.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. We knocked across.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "set off/set out" or simply "went out early" — "knocked across" is not a valid expression. The intended meaning ("started out early") requires a proper verb; "We set off" is correct. Hence segment (1) contains the error. (यह मुहावरा ग़लत है)

◦ Correct: We set off early on Saturday to enjoy the beautiful weather.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "early on Saturday", "to enjoy" and "the beautiful weather" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Common "knock" phrasal verbs: knock off (stop work), knock out (make unconscious), knock down (demolish). There is no standard "knock across".

question:
Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

The interns explained the whole issue to the coordinator in a nutshell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. in a brief manner.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "in a nutshell" means in a very brief and concise way; in a few words. So it can be substituted by "in a brief manner". (संक्षेप में)

◦ Example: To put it in a nutshell, the project failed due to poor planning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "in a secret way", 3 "in an uncertain way" and 4 "in a discouraging manner" do not convey brevity.

NOTE

• Similar expressions of brevity: "in short", "in brief", "to sum up", "in a word", "to cut a long story short".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Credeble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Credeble" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "credible", meaning believable or trustworthy. (विश्वसनीय)

◦ Spelling key: CRED + I + BLE (credible).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Devoted" (dedicated), "Explosive" (able to explode) and "Creative" (imaginative) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Do not confuse credible (believable) with credulous (too ready to believe) and creditable (deserving praise).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

Adi had not only assisted her by giving evidence in the case but also provided many examples to prove her point in the court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. assisted her not only by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the correlative "not only ... but also", the structure after "not only" must be parallel with the structure after "but also". Here "but also provided..." begins with a verb-phrase describing a means, so "not only" should precede the corresponding phrase "by giving evidence". The object "her" must come right after the verb "assisted". Hence: "assisted her not only by giving evidence ... but also provided ...". (समानांतर संरचना)

◦ Correct: Adi had assisted her not only by giving evidence in the case but also provided many examples ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other options either misplace the object "her" or break the parallelism required by "not only ... but also".

NOTE

• Rule of parallelism: the words/phrases that follow "not only" and "but also" must be grammatically the same in form (verb with verb, phrase with phrase).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

A buzzing ______ can ____ dangerous.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. bee; be.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs a noun — a "buzzing bee" (the insect). The second blank needs the verb "be" — "can be dangerous". So the pair is "bee; be". (मधुमक्खी; होना)

◦ Correct: A buzzing bee can be dangerous.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "bee" (insect) vs "be" (verb of existence) are homophones.

• "deer" (animal) and "dear" (beloved/expensive) in the other options do not fit the sentence.

NOTE

• Homophones are words that sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning: bee/be, deer/dear, sea/see, right/write, hear/here.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. truth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "accepted as gospel truth" is a fixed expression meaning accepted as absolutely true, beyond doubt. Directors accepted "as gospel truth" that the audience should not be taxed too much. (परम सत्य के रूप में स्वीकार करना)

◦ Correct: ... had accepted as gospel truth that the audience should not be taxed too much.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "blasphemy" (irreverence towards the sacred) is the opposite in tone.

• Options 3 "followers" and 4 "Bible" do not fit the collocation "gospel ___".

NOTE

• "Gospel truth" = something completely and unquestionably true. To "take something as gospel" means to believe it without doubt.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. blow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The expression "strike a blow at" means to attack or take strong action against something. Welles "struck a blow at these beliefs" — i.e., he attacked the established conventions. "Blow" (a noun) is needed after "struck a". (प्रहार करना)

◦ Correct: Welles struck a blow at these beliefs ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "blew" (past tense of blow) and Option 3 "bellow" (to shout loudly) are verbs and do not fit after "struck a".

• Option 4 "blue" (a colour) is irrelevant.

NOTE

• "Strike a blow for/against" is an idiom: to act decisively in support of, or against, a cause or belief.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. permeated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Permeated" means spread throughout; pervaded. The harsh sharpness "permeated every scene" — i.e., it filled and spread across every scene of the film. (हर दृश्य में व्याप्त होना)

◦ Correct: ... shot with a harsh sharpness which permeated every scene.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "promoted" (encouraged), Option 2 "permitted" (allowed) and Option 3 "prevented" (stopped) do not convey the sense of the sharpness spreading through every scene.

NOTE

• Synonyms of permeate: pervade, spread through, saturate, suffuse, infuse. It suggests something filling every part of an area or thing.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. eye.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "keep an eye on" means to watch carefully; to monitor closely. Make-up men and cameramen had to "keep a careful eye on" the heroine's appearance. (नज़र रखना)

◦ Correct: ... had to keep a careful eye on the appearance of the heroine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "nose", 3 "ear" and 4 "leg" do not form the fixed idiom "keep an eye on".

NOTE

• Related "eye" idioms: "keep an eye on" (monitor), "catch someone's eye" (attract attention), "turn a blind eye" (ignore), "see eye to eye" (agree).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Until that moment, every director in Hollywood had accepted as gospel (1)_______ that the audience should not be taxed too much. Welles struck a (2)_______ at these beliefs, without displaying the slightest of qualms. Visually, 'Citizen Kane' was shot with a harsh sharpness which (3)_____ every scene. Traditionally, every make-up man and cameraman in Hollywood had to keep a careful (4)_______ on the appearance of the heroine. Welles refused to follow this (5)_____ in the case of his own heroine. For the first time, dialogue was presented in its realistic form.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. practice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A noun is required after "this" to refer back to the traditional custom just described. "Practice" (noun) means a customary way of doing something; a habit or convention. Welles refused to follow this practice. (प्रथा / रीति)

◦ Correct: Welles refused to follow this practice in the case of his own heroine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "practise" is the verb (British spelling) and cannot follow "this".

• Option 1 "practicals" and Option 3 "prose" do not fit the meaning.

NOTE

• In British English: "practice" is the noun (a good practice) and "practise" is the verb (to practise daily). In American English, "practice" is used for both.

question: The 9th Asian Games was hosted by which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 9th Asian Games were hosted by India, held in New Delhi in 1982. This was the second time India hosted the Asian Games (the 1st Asian Games were also held in New Delhi in 1951). (9वें एशियाई खेल — भारत, 1982)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The mascot of the 1982 Asian Games was "Appu", an elephant.

• The Asian Games are held every four years and are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

NOTE

• The 19th Asian Games were held in Hangzhou, China (2023), where India won a record 107 medals. The first Asian Games (1951) were also in New Delhi.

question: A child is a picky eater. He does not consume milk at all and barely eats other kinds of food. When he started losing his baby teeth, they were not getting replaced with new teeth. This can be solved by giving him ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is calcium supplements.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Since the child avoids milk (a rich source of calcium) and his teeth are not being replaced, the problem is a calcium deficiency. Giving calcium supplements will help proper tooth and bone development. (कैल्शियम की कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Calcium is essential for strong bones and teeth, blood clotting and muscle function.

• The absorption of calcium is aided by Vitamin D; its deficiency causes weak bones (rickets/osteomalacia).

NOTE

• Rich sources of calcium: milk, cheese, curd, green leafy vegetables, ragi and sesame seeds.

question: An Indian Parliamentary delegation led by Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines ______________________ visited Brazil from 11 to 13 June 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pralhad Joshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pralhad Joshi, the then Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines, led an Indian Parliamentary delegation that visited Brazil from 11 to 13 June 2023. (प्रह्लाद जोशी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pralhad Joshi represents the Dharwad constituency of Karnataka in the Lok Sabha.

• Such parliamentary delegations promote inter-parliamentary cooperation and bilateral relations.

NOTE

• Brazil is a member of the BRICS grouping (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa) along with India. Its capital is Brasília.

question: Kala Ramnath belonged to which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mewati gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kala Ramnath, a renowned Indian violinist in Hindustani classical music, belongs to the Mewati gharana. She comes from a family of musicians and is known for her "singing violin" style. (मेवाती घराना — काला रामनाथ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A "gharana" is a system of social organisation in Indian classical music linking musicians by lineage or style.

• The Mewati gharana is also associated with the legendary vocalist Pandit Jasraj.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala and Mewati.

question: Anuradhapura, the old capital of Sri Lanka, was destroyed by which of the following dynasties of South India in the 10th century AD?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anuradhapura, the ancient capital of Sri Lanka, was invaded and destroyed by the Chola dynasty of South India in the 10th century AD (under rulers such as Rajaraja I and Rajendra I). (चोल वंश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Cholas were a powerful South Indian dynasty known for their strong navy and overseas conquests, including Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia.

• Rajaraja Chola I built the famous Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeswaram) Temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• The Chola capital was Thanjavur (Tanjore). Rajendra Chola I founded a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, after his victories up to the Ganga.

question: As per Article 157 of the Constitution of India, a person needs to complete the age of ____________ years to be appointed as Governor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 35.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Article 157 of the Constitution of India, a person must have completed the age of 35 years to be eligible for appointment as the Governor of a state. (राज्यपाल — न्यूनतम आयु 35 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other qualifications under Article 157–158: the person must be a citizen of India and must not hold any office of profit.

• The Governor is appointed by the President (Article 155) and holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156).

NOTE

• Minimum age comparisons: Governor / MP (Lok Sabha) – 25 (Lok Sabha) but Governor 35; President / Vice-President / Rajya Sabha member – 35 years; MLA – 25 years.

question: Which writ is issued by the High Court or Supreme Court when a lower court considers a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prohibition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The writ of "Prohibition" is issued by a higher court (High Court or Supreme Court) to a lower court or tribunal to stop it from proceeding in a case that is beyond its jurisdiction. (निषेध / प्रोहिबिशन)

• It literally means "to forbid" and is issued while proceedings are pending.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Habeas Corpus – "to have the body"; against unlawful detention.

• Mandamus – "we command"; directs a public official/body to perform its duty.

• Quo Warranto – "by what authority"; questions a person's right to hold a public office.

• Certiorari – "to be certified"; quashes an order already passed by a lower court.

NOTE

• Writs are issued under Article 32 (by the Supreme Court) and Article 226 (by the High Courts). Article 226 has a wider scope than Article 32.

question: Every year, Karthik Purnima marks the end of a livestock fair in Pushkar, where the main animal on display is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is camel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Pushkar Fair (Pushkar Mela) in Rajasthan, which ends on Kartik Purnima, is renowned as a camel fair, where thousands of camels are traded and displayed. (पुष्कर मेला — ऊँट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Pushkar is located in the Ajmer district of Rajasthan and is famous for the Brahma Temple, one of the very few temples dedicated to Lord Brahma.

• The fair features camel races, decorations, cultural performances and a large religious gathering at the sacred Pushkar Lake.

NOTE

• The camel is the state animal of Rajasthan. Rajasthan's other famous fair is the Nagaur Cattle Fair.

question: Which of the following organisations in India provides facilities for acquisition of satellite data and its processing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) provides facilities for the acquisition and processing of satellite data in India. It is a centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), headquartered at Hyderabad. (राष्ट्रीय सुदूर संवेदन केंद्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The NRSC operates the ground station at Shadnagar for receiving remote-sensing satellite data and is responsible for aerial remote sensing and disaster management support.

• The Indian Institute of Remote Sensing (IIRS), Dehradun, is mainly a training and education institute (also under ISRO).

NOTE

• ISRO was founded in 1969; its headquarters is at Bengaluru and it is led by a Chairman. Its first satellite was Aryabhata (1975).

question: Which of the following Indian cities was the host of the ICC Men's World Cup final cricket match in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 was hosted at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, Gujarat — the world's largest cricket stadium. (अहमदाबाद — नरेंद्र मोदी स्टेडियम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In the 2023 final, Australia defeated India to win their 6th World Cup title. India remained unbeaten until the final.

• Virat Kohli was the Player of the Tournament, and Australia's Travis Head was Player of the Match in the final.

NOTE

• The 2023 ODI World Cup was hosted entirely by India. India's previous World Cup wins: 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M. S. Dhoni).

question: Which of the following is included in the estimation of Gross National Product?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sale of new shirts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only the value of newly produced final goods and services is included in national income (GNP). The "sale of new shirts" represents current production and is therefore counted in GNP. (नए उत्पादित माल — जीएनपी में शामिल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pension payments are transfer payments (no production involved) — excluded.

• Sale of securities (shares/bonds) is a financial transaction, not production — excluded.

• Sale of used cars was already counted when the car was first produced — excluded (to avoid double counting).

NOTE

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). National income accounting counts only final goods, avoiding intermediate goods and transfer payments.

question: When was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre brought into action by the Britishers in Amritsar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 April, 1919.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 at Amritsar, Punjab, on the day of Baisakhi. General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful, unarmed gathering, killing and wounding hundreds. (जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड — 13 अप्रैल 1919)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The crowd had gathered to protest against the Rowlatt Act (1919) and the arrest of leaders Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.

• In protest, Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood, and Udham Singh later assassinated Michael O'Dwyer (in 1940) in London.

NOTE

• The Hunter Commission was set up to inquire into the massacre. Sir Shankaran Nair resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council in protest.

question: In January 2023, the Chief Minister's Residential Land Rights Scheme (Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana) was launched in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mukhyamantri Awasiya Bhu Adhikar Yojana (Chief Minister's Residential Land Rights Scheme)" was launched in Madhya Pradesh (in January 2023) to provide residential plots/land rights to the landless poor. (मध्य प्रदेश — मुख्यमंत्री आवासीय भू-अधिकार योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme aims to grant free residential land to eligible landless families who do not own a house or plot in the state.

• The capital of Madhya Pradesh is Bhopal; it is the second-largest state of India by area.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh is known as the "Heart of India" (Hindustan ka Dil) and has the largest tiger population among Indian states.

question: The Citadel area has a huge mud ________ platform, which is 6 m high and underlies all the construction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is brick.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Harappan (Indus Valley) cities, the Citadel was built on a huge mud-brick platform, about 6 metres high, on which all the constructions rested. This raised the Citadel above the lower town. (मिट्टी की ईंट का चबूतरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Harappan towns had two parts: the Citadel (higher, western part, with important buildings like the Great Bath and Granary) and the Lower Town (residential area).

• Harappans used standardised baked bricks in the ratio 4:2:1 (length:breadth:height).

NOTE

• Major Harappan sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan and Rakhigarhi. The civilization was discovered in 1921 (Harappa).

question: Who is the author of the English novel 'Voting at Fosterganj'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The English novel "Voting at Fosterganj" was written by the celebrated author Ruskin Bond, known for his stories set in the hills of North India. (रस्किन बॉन्ड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ruskin Bond was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award (1992) for "Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra", the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014).

• His famous works include "The Room on the Roof", "The Blue Umbrella" and "A Flight of Pigeons".

NOTE

• "The Blue Umbrella" and "A Flight of Pigeons" (as *Junoon*) were adapted into Hindi films. Ruskin Bond lives in Landour, Mussoorie.

question: The revival of the art form in the late 1940s was spearheaded by maestros such as Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta in the field of ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The revival of the classical dance form "Odissi" in the late 1940s was led by maestros such as Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta. Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha. (ओडिसी नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Odissi is characterised by the tribhanga (three-bend) posture and chauka stance, and depicts themes from the Jayadeva's Gita Govinda.

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary Odissi guru who received the Padma Vibhushan.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (North), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: The Indus Water Treaty took place in ________ between India and Pakistan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1960.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan, brokered by the World Bank. It was signed by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi. (सिंधु जल संधि — 1960)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Under the treaty, the waters of the three eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — were allocated to India.

• The three western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab — were allocated largely to Pakistan (India can use them for limited purposes).

NOTE

• The Indus river system has six main rivers. A useful mnemonic for eastern rivers (India's) is "R-B-S" (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).

question: Kanaka Raju, who kept the tribal folk dance Gussadi alive, was honoured with which of the following civilian awards of India in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Shri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kanaka Raju, who kept the tribal folk dance "Gussadi" of the Gond tribe alive, was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2021. (पद्म श्री — कनक राजू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Gussadi dance is performed by the Gond tribe of Telangana during the Dandari festival.

• The Padma Awards are announced on Republic Day, in three categories — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri (in decreasing order of importance).

NOTE

• Highest civilian awards order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954.

question: What is the atomic number of uranium (U)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 92.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The atomic number of uranium (U) is 92, meaning it has 92 protons in its nucleus. Uranium is a radioactive metal used as nuclear fuel. (यूरेनियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 92)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Uranium is a naturally occurring radioactive element; its important isotopes are U-235 (fissile, used in reactors and bombs) and U-238.

• Uranium is placed in the actinide series of the periodic table.

NOTE

• Some atomic numbers to remember: Hydrogen 1, Carbon 6, Oxygen 8, Iron 26, Uranium 92, Plutonium 94. Rutherfordium has atomic number 104.

question: What was the unemployment rate of Gujarat in November 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.4%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to CMIE (Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy) data, Gujarat had one of the lowest unemployment rates in India at about 1.4% in November 2021. (गुजरात — बेरोज़गारी दर 1.4%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The unemployment rate is the percentage of the labour force that is jobless but actively seeking work.

• In India, employment/unemployment data is compiled by the CMIE and through the government's Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) by the NSO.

NOTE

• A low unemployment rate indicates a higher share of the workforce being employed. Gujarat's capital is Gandhinagar; its largest city is Ahmedabad.

question: Which of the following periods in India is also associated with the Iron Age?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Later Vedic Age.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Later Vedic Age" (c. 1000–600 BCE) in India is associated with the Iron Age, as the use of iron (called "Krishna Ayas" or "Shyama Ayas") became widespread during this period. (उत्तर वैदिक काल — लौह युग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Iron implements helped clear the dense forests of the Gangetic plains and enabled the expansion of agriculture and larger kingdoms.

• The archaeological culture linked with iron in this period is the Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture.

NOTE

• Prehistoric ages by material: Palaeolithic → Mesolithic → Neolithic (Stone Age) → Chalcolithic (Copper) → Bronze (Harappan) → Iron Age (Later Vedic).

question: As per Census 2011, which of the following states has the lowest child sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, Haryana had the lowest child sex ratio (0–6 years) among the states, at 834 girls per 1000 boys. (हरियाणा — सबसे कम बाल लिंगानुपात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Child sex ratio is the number of girls per 1000 boys in the 0–6 age group.

• India's overall sex ratio (2011) was 943 females per 1000 males; Kerala had the highest (1084) and Haryana the lowest among the major states.

NOTE

• To improve the declining child sex ratio, the government launched the "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" scheme in 2015 from Panipat, Haryana.

question: Tsunami is a natural disaster that originates from the ocean. The cause of Tsunami in the ocean is:
option_1: The movement of tectonic plates under the ocean
option_2: The alarmingly increasing amount of acid in water
option_3: The presence of excessive carbon dioxide in the water
option_4: The accumulation of high amount of radioactive pollutants in the ocean
solution_text:
The correct answer is The movement of tectonic plates under the ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A tsunami is caused mainly by the sudden movement of tectonic plates under the ocean (an undersea earthquake), which displaces a large volume of water and generates giant waves. (सुनामी — समुद्र के नीचे विवर्तनिक प्लेटों की गति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tsunamis can also be triggered by undersea volcanic eruptions, landslides or large meteorite impacts.

• The word "tsunami" is Japanese, meaning "harbour wave".

NOTE

• The devastating Indian Ocean Tsunami of 26 December 2004 was caused by a massive earthquake off Sumatra, Indonesia, and severely affected India's Tamil Nadu and Andaman coasts.

question: The planned large-scale disruption of rail communications and the seizure of arms in Bengal were undertaken under the leadership of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jatin Mukherjee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The planned large-scale disruption of rail communications and seizure of arms in Bengal were undertaken under the leadership of Jatin Mukherjee (Bagha Jatin), a leading revolutionary of the Jugantar party. (जतिन मुखर्जी — बाघा जतिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bagha Jatin was involved in the Indo-German Conspiracy (Zimmerman Plan) during World War I, aiming to import German arms to start an armed uprising.

• He died fighting the British in the Battle of Balasore (1915) in Odisha.

NOTE

• Bengal's revolutionary organisations included Anushilan Samiti and Jugantar. He earned the name "Bagha Jatin" ("Tiger Jatin") for killing a tiger with a dagger.

question: Select the INCORRECT statement regarding Ozone.
option_1: Ozone is formed from oxygen in the presence of ultraviolet radiation.
option_2: Ozone (O3), like oxygen, is a life-supporting gas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ozone (O3), like oxygen, is a life-supporting gas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This statement is INCORRECT. Unlike oxygen (O₂), which supports life through respiration, ozone (O₃) is NOT a life-supporting (respirable) gas — it is actually toxic/poisonous to breathe. In the stratosphere it is beneficial (shields us from UV), but it does not support breathing. (ओज़ोन जीवनरक्षक श्वसन गैस नहीं है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Statement 1 is correct: ozone forms when UV radiation splits O₂, and free oxygen atoms combine with O₂ to form O₃.

• Statement 3 is correct: excessive UV radiation causes skin cancer, cataracts, etc.

• Statement 4 is correct: ozone at ground level is a poisonous gas and a pollutant.

NOTE

• The ozone layer in the stratosphere protects the Earth from harmful UV rays. 16 September is observed as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer (linked to the Montreal Protocol, 1987).
